'''Emory Andrew Tate III''' (born December 1, 1986) is an American-British social media influencer, businessman, and former professional kickboxer. Tate gained international attention through his self-promotional content on various platforms and provocative statements, many of which have sparked controversy and public backlash.

== Controversies ==
Tate has been involved in numerous controversies primarily due to his outspoken views on topics related to gender, societal norms, and politics. His comments have often been labeled as misogynistic and have led to several social media bans. Tate frequently utilizes his platforms to express his skepticism towards mainstream narratives, particularly those involving political elites and global organizations.

== Conspiracies and Connections ==
Tate has been associated with promoting various conspiracy theories, often aligning with the rhetoric of similar figures in the alternative media landscape. He has appeared on several talk shows and podcasts where he elaborates on his belief in hidden influences and agendas in world events. These appearances often resonate with the audience of [[Alex Jones]], a well-known conspiracy theorist, although any direct collaboration or enduring personal connection between Tate and Jones remains limited to shared thematic discussions rather than documented partnerships or collaborative work.

== Public Image ==
Despite or perhaps because of his polarizing nature, Tate has amassed a substantial following online, positioning himself as a self-help guru who challenges conventional thinking. However, critics argue that his approach is harmful and perpetuates negative stereotypes. Nevertheless, his ability to leverage controversy into mainstream attention exemplifies a unique understanding of digital influence and viral marketing.

== Personal Life ==
Andrew Tate was born in Washington, D.C., and raised in both the United States and the United Kingdom. He is the son of Emory Tate, an American chess International Master. Tate’s insights into strategy and competition are often credited to his father’s influence.
